problems.detail: The bound gate is not deterministic on first attempt. My first dispatcher replay FAILED (invocation 526d6cf4..., exit 1, 8 assertions, A8 detail: {'host_health':'DOWN','host_url':'http://127.0.0.1:18923','electron':'37.10.3'}), and it passed only on retry 1 (ff3d1863..., exit 0, 9 assertions). This is not a dead host and not a proxy artifact: over 25 shell launches against a live isolated host on my own ports/data dir, 5 reported DOWN, and at the failing instants urllib GET on the same URL returned 200, netstat still showed the LISTENING socket, the host child process poll was alive and the host log held only the single 'listening' line; 25 back-to-back requests from Electron's own bundled Node all returned 200 in 1-6 ms, and a dispatcher-like whitelisted environment (no HTTP_PROXY/NO_PROXY, build.check's allowed_env contains no proxy key) still reproduced the DOWN 3 times out of 8. So main.js's single-shot probe intermittently sees a client-side connection error against a healthy host. Aggravating factor: the ROS_DESKTOP_REPORT line omits the probe's error field (main.js:40 keeps only health/url/electron/protocol/pid), and A8 keeps only the report plus empty stderr, so a failure of this assertion is not diagnosable from the invocation receipt. Required before this handler is reused for the parent gate: (a) include the resolved error/code (and elapsed ms) in ROS_DESKTOP_REPORT, (b) make the probe bounded-retry (e.g. 3 attempts, 300-500 ms apart) instead of single-shot, (c) re-run dispatch build.check --check-id W02-03 several times and record the observed pass rate. The card's own deliverable is unaffected in substance - the window really boots and the probe really speaks HTTP - which is why this is a hardening requirement rather than a rejection; but a gate that flips green/red on the same input cannot be treated as a reproducible PASS for W02-99.

The new entry registers check_id ['W02-03','W02-99'], but the parent card's gate commands in the plan invoke build.check with check_id W02-G01 / W02-G02 / W02-G03 and expect assertion ids named W02-G0x, which this handler can never emit; 'W02-99' is therefore a selector no registered command will ever route to, and it slightly overstates reusability of this handler for parent acceptance beyond the card's 'registers this exact selector' mandate. Related disclosure gap: the receipt does not mention that six UNBOUND entries still name owner_card 'W02-03' (fork.install_deps, fork.build_worker, fork.worker_launch_rpc, fork.worker_stop, cli.entry_run, desktop.shell_launch) while W02 has no card left after W02-03 except W02-99. That is consistent with the thin-entry scope (the card's own verification command is only build.check) but the ownership hand-off must be stated and re-assigned by the W02 registry owner before the parent gates.

problems.detail: Card step 1 asks for a ResearchOS 名称/图标/构建入口. Name (productName 'researchos', BrowserWindow title 'ResearchOS', window identity 'researchos-desktop') and build entry are delivered; the 图标 is not - there is no .ico/.png under apps/ and BrowserWindow is created without an icon option, so the launched window carries Electron's default icon. Likewise the '上游已有CLI启动器' is not attached yet (main.go states the Mu/Pi starter is attached later; nothing in apps/cli invokes upstream code). Neither omission is a counterexample under the card's NEGATIVE clause, but they are not listed in remaining_blocks either, so the receipt understates what step 1 left open.

Two assertions are weaker than their labels. A7_DOCTOR_HANDSHAKE asserts j['host_pid'] == host_proc.pid, but the handler itself wrote that pid into .local/v24_host.json one line earlier, so the pid equality is self-attested; the only independent content is health UP plus the client_protocol string, and the host never echoes a protocol id (internal/api/server.go /healthz returns {status,scope,database} only). A9_SHUTDOWN_ISOLATION hashes 'old data root' as only the files under .local/data whose name contains 'lock' or whose suffix is exactly '.sqlite', and only their first 64 KiB - .local/data contains no lock file and the -wal/-shm siblings are outside the set, so the receipt wording 'old data-root files byte-identical' overstates the helper's coverage. I closed both gaps by hand (full-file sha256 of all 4 files including -wal/-shm unchanged, and my own live-host doctor run), so the conclusions stand.

limitations.detail: The shared discovery contract is asymmetric: the CLI reads the CWD-relative path '.local/v24_host.json' while the shell resolves an absolute module-relative path to the repository root. They agree only when the CLI is run from the repository root; `researchos doctor` from any other directory reports NOT_FOUND exit 3 even with a healthy host. Acceptable for a thin development entry, must become a real per-user path (blueprint 19 §5 item 1) before any product claim.

What is verified is: both clients discover the host through the same file, issue a real HTTP GET /healthz, and display their own declared protocol id researchos-client/2 plus host liveness/pid/data_dir. What is NOT implemented is negotiation - the host has no protocol field, no UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL path and no rejection of a /1 client (doc 22 §1), which the registry attributes to protocol.v2_roundtrip (UNBOUND, owner W03+). The card only asks Desktop to display 宿主状态和协议版本 and CLI doctor to give real feedback, so the increment is compliant, but 'version handshake' must not be read as negotiated compatibility.

build_check.py hard-codes .local/tools/go1.27.1/go/bin/go.exe instead of using the RESEARCHOS_GO path the dispatcher injects from execution/toolchains/locked.json (the dispatcher does hash-verify that locked go on every run, so the pinned toolchain is enforced independently of this shortcut; the handler is just less portable than it could be). The Electron tarball resolved from registry.npmmirror.com rather than registry.npmjs.org; I established binary integrity independently by re-hashing the cached official zip against the package's own checksums.json, but the install source is a mirror and no registry pin exists in the card scope.

limitations.detail: I verified the shell in ROS_DESKTOP_SMOKE=1 mode (hidden window, exits after 300 ms) and via the IPC/preload surface in code; I did not capture a screenshot of a visible window, did not drive the rendered page as a user, did not test the single-worker chain or any worker launch (fork.* still UNBOUND), did not test installer/packaging (W16), and did not exercise an interactive TUI (owned by W03/W05). The P1 flake rate estimate is 5 DOWN / 25 live-host launches (~20%) from my own samples, not a long-run measurement; the underlying layer (why Electron's main-process request errors against a healthy loopback listener) is not root-caused, only isolated to the client side.

The checkpoint is still at revision 14 with head ee58a389 (a W00-era commit) and next_step_id W02-03, i.e. it has not been advanced by W02-01/02/03. checkpoint.json is outside this card's write scope, so this is not a W02-03 violation, but the card's 下一步 expects a checkpoint update and the orchestrator/integrator owes that revision (including the failing-attempt count for A8) before the next card is picked.

summary: ACCEPT. The claim is real work, not a mock: I rebuilt both Go binaries myself with the locked go1.27.1 (GOTOOLCHAIN=local), observed version/help/doctor/chat behaving exactly as reported including non-zero exits 3/3/4/3 for the negative paths, watched the CLI doctor reach a host I started on my own port with my own data dir, watched the shipped Electron 37.10.3 window boot with a constrained one-method preload and report host_health UP plus protocol researchos-client/2, verified the official electron-v37.10.3-win32-x64.zip by re-hashing it (af69b8a4... == checksums.json, so targeted_repair_1 is truthful), confirmed node_modules is untracked (0 files) and the lockfile pins 37.10.3 exactly, confirmed the old 8787 stayed closed and every byte and mtime under .local/data is untouched (newest 2026-09-30), and confirmed the commands.json write is append-only with an explicit revision_note and registry disclosure (rev1 bf8de03b -> rev2 daf398d3, 0 old keys changed, and the plan itself mandates key build.check). The binding gate reproduced the recorded PASS field-for-field, byte-identical stdout (26577f3f...), registry_spec v2.4 and 9 assertions - but only on retry: my first replay failed A8 because main.js's single-shot health probe intermittently reports DOWN against a provably live host (5 of 25 launches, dispatcher-whitelisted env, no proxy involved) and the ROS_DESKTOP_REPORT omits the error code, so the failure is un-diagnosable from the receipt. That is P1 and must be hardened (surface error, bounded retry, report the observed pass rate) before build.check is reused for W02-99; P2-P4 are the unexplained W02-99 selector plus six still-UNBOUND entries owned by W02-03, the missing ResearchOS icon and unwired upstream CLI starter, and the self-attested A7 pid check and narrow A9 hash set. Limitations L1-L5 record the CWD-relative CLI discovery, the one-sided (non-negotiated) protocol handshake, the hard-coded go path and mirror install source, the surfaces I did not exercise, and the stale checkpoint that the integrator still owes. No executor self-acceptance, no A04/C23 or parent-level claim: step_state keeps W02-03 at EXECUTION_REPORTED with verifier_id null.
